questions.prompt: The old wolf was good at catching birds and rabbits.
questions.evidenceSnippet: The hungry old wolf was too slow to snatch birds and too stiff to chase rabbits, so he tried growing food in a small garden.
questions.evidenceHighlight: too slow to snatch birds and too stiff to chase rabbits

questions.prompt: What did the old wolf find in the clearing?
questions.evidenceSnippet: After a tiring climb and two stubbed toes, the old wolf came to a clearing. “What's this? A boy? With goats!"

questions.prompt: The boy called "WOLF! WOLF!" because a wolf was really taking his goats.
questions.evidenceSnippet: "What wolf?" the boy giggled. "There is no wolf."

questions.prompt: Was the wolf's trick to scare the boy and make him stop yelling "Wolf!"?
questions.evidenceSnippet: "The villagers are only going to believe you if you really are missing a goat. I can help you with that." He grinned. "Just one goat?" The boy leaned forward on the branch. "I'm a picky eater. That plump one looks about right. But you have to bring it to me, because if I go over there, I might change my mind and grab them all."
questions.evidenceHighlight: The villagers are only going to believe you if you really are missing a goat. I can help you with that.

questions.prompt: What surprising thing did the old wolf find in his garden?
choices: The garden was full of weeds again
The garden was full of ripe vegetables
The boy was hiding in the garden
questions.evidenceSnippet: Everywhere he looked, there were ripe and juicy vegetables: baby bok choy, beautiful eggplant, ready-to-pick carrots, and even his favorite—onions.
questions.evidenceHighlight: Everywhere he looked, there were ripe and juicy vegetables

questions.prompt: At the end of the story, the wolf decided to eat the goat.
questions.evidenceSnippet: "Don't be sorry! You did my work for me. What's one breakfast compared to delicious vegetables for the rest of my days?" The wolf smiled as he untied the goat. "I could use a friend like you."
